exam.title: Social Studies Paper 1 (15/1) - October/November 2021
exam.subject: Social Studies
exam.description: Botswana Examinations Council, Junior Certificate Examination. Answer all 40 questions. Four possible answers are given for each; choose the one you think is correct.

questions.question: Which element of weather is measured using a barometer?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric (air) pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following activities is likely to be practised by people living in a desert environment?
questions.explanation: Deserts attract wildlife and scenic tourism (e.g. the Kalahari); fishing and large-scale farming are not practical there.

questions.question: Which of the following climatic regions does not experience seasonal changes?
questions.explanation: Equatorial regions have a fairly constant temperature and rainfall pattern all year round, with no distinct seasons.

questions.question:
A certain climatic region experiences heavy rainfall every year. The rain comes in summer and is caused by strong moist winds that blow from the ocean towards land.

Which of the following crops would be easy to grow in this region?
questions.explanation: Rice needs abundant water and thrives with heavy seasonal rainfall, unlike apples, grapes and beans which prefer drier conditions.

questions.question:
Lesego and three of her friends are unemployed youth. They each decided to set-up stalls to sell fruits and vegetables in front of a shopping centre in their neighbourhood.

What is likely to be the main challenge for Lesego and her friends as they try to sell their goods in front of the shopping centre?
questions.explanation: With four friends all selling the same fruit and vegetables in the same spot, they will be competing for the same customers.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions can Lesego and her friends approach for financial assistance to start a formal business?
questions.explanation: The Citizen Entrepreneurial Development Agency (CEDA) provides funding and support to citizen-owned businesses in Botswana.

questions.question: Which of the following factors contribute to human resource development?
questions.explanation: Quality tertiary education builds the skills and knowledge that make up a country's human resources.

questions.question: Which of the following workers is engaged in the informal sector?
questions.explanation: Hawkers operate outside formal registration and regulation, which is the hallmark of informal-sector work.

questions.question: Which of the following is a statutory bank in Botswana?
questions.explanation: The Bank of Botswana is a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament to act as the country's central bank.

questions.question:
A steel manufacturing company in Botswana makes and supplies steel to Orapa mine for use in the production of diamonds.

Which aspect has Orapa mine created for the steel company?
questions.explanation: By buying the steel it needs, Orapa mine gives the steel company a market for its product.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an importance of craters to human beings?
questions.explanation: Craters can attract tourists, hold minerals and collect water, but they are not generally used as a means of defence.

questions.question: Which of the following is the responsibility of government at local level?
questions.explanation: Local government (councils) is responsible for local services such as refuse collection; security, major roads and national law-making sit with central government.

questions.question:
Country W is threatening to attack country X for allowing citizens from country W to take refuge in it.

Which branch of the United Nations is mandated to condemn the actions of country W?
questions.explanation: The Security Council is the UN body mandated to respond to threats to international peace and security.

questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the Judiciary as a branch of government?
questions.explanation: The Judiciary's role is to interpret and apply the law; making laws is the Legislature's role and implementing policy is the Executive's.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a civil responsibility of citizens in Botswana?
questions.explanation: Returning faulty goods is a consumer right/action, not a civic responsibility like voting, protecting property or paying tax.

questions.question: Which sector of production does a bank fall under?
questions.explanation: Banks provide a service rather than extracting or manufacturing goods, which places them in the tertiary sector.

questions.question: What is the name of the mining town labelled X?
questions.explanation: X marks the location of Jwaneng, Botswana's major diamond-mining town in the south-central part of the country.

questions.question: What major environmental problem can be caused by the mining activity at Z?
questions.explanation: Z marks a coal-mining site; dust and smoke from coal mining and its processing are a major source of air pollution.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of the processing of the mineral found at Y?
questions.explanation: Soda ash ore is first crushed, then graded by size, then refined to purify it.

questions.question:
Every year the city of Mombasa in Kenya hosts the Mombasa Carnival. This is a carnival of costumes, food, music and dance that showcases the country's cultural diversity. Participants dress in traditional Kikoyo and Kanga.

Which of the following is not depicted in the information above?
questions.explanation: Food shows diet, costumes show dress, and music/dance show entertainment — technology is not mentioned.

questions.question: Which tool is associated with Homo erectus?
questions.explanation: The Acheulian hand-axe tradition is associated with Homo erectus.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the Egyptian and Mesopotamian civilisations?
options: They both had leaders who have divine powers.
They both lived in the city states surrounded by small villages.
questions.explanation: Both Egyptian pharaohs and Mesopotamian rulers were regarded as having divine or god-given authority.

questions.question: Which statement below does not describe the way of life of the Nguni people before the arrival of the Europeans?
options: They relied on livestock for livelihood.
They lived in a place for a short period of time.
questions.explanation: The Nguni lived in fairly settled, dispersed homesteads under their chiefs and depended on cattle — they were not short-term or nomadic settlers.

questions.question: Which Tswana group defeated the Boers at Kgwakgwe Hills in 1852?
questions.explanation: The Bakwena, led by Kgosi Sechele I, defeated the Boers near Kgwakgwe Hills (Dimawe) in 1852.

questions.question: Which of the following is an impact of the early traders and hunters on the lives of Batswana?
questions.explanation: Contact with early traders and hunters drew Batswana men into labour migration in search of wages and trade goods.

questions.question:
Mmusi wanted to know about his tribe. He visited his grandparents who shared with him stories of the past about his tribe.

What source of information did Mmusi use?
questions.explanation: Stories passed down and told by elders are oral history.

questions.question: The growth of nationalism in Bechuanaland was shown by
options: educated Batswana asking for protection from the British.
dikgosi supporting racial discrimination in Bechuanaland.
dikgosi agreeing to reduction of their powers.
questions.explanation: Educated Batswana organising themselves into political parties was a direct expression of a growing national political consciousness.

questions.question: Which group is responsible for spreading iron working technology into Southern Africa?
questions.explanation: Bantu-speaking migrants brought iron-working technology into Southern Africa during their migrations.

questions.question: Which of the following was one of the terms of the Sand River Convention of 1852?
options: The British would protect the Boers against Tswana
Batswana would buy guns from the Boers
The Boers would rule the Transvaal state
questions.explanation: The Sand River Convention recognised the independence of the Boers north of the Vaal River, i.e. their right to govern the Transvaal.

questions.question: Which factor contributes to a decrease in a country's population?
questions.explanation: Emigration removes people from a country's population, reducing its size; the other options all tend to increase population.

questions.question: Which of the following is the role of community leaders in the welfare of the Youth?
options: Providing training opportunities for the youth
Providing basic needs to the youth
questions.explanation: At community level, leaders such as dikgosi typically encourage and support local activities like youth sport; large-scale training, funding and welfare provision are handled by national bodies.

questions.question:
Mr and Mrs Kaelo are preparing for the wedding of their son Tebo who is getting married to Moipone. Tebo's parents will be taking a herd of 8 cattle as lobola to Moipone's house which is located behind Roman Catholic Church.

Which family member is expected to lead the marriage negotiations?
questions.explanation: In Setswana custom, a senior paternal uncle (malome) traditionally leads the lobola negotiations on behalf of the family.

questions.question: What type of marriage is Tebo and Moipone getting into?
questions.explanation: Paying lobola (bogadi/bride cattle) to the bride's family is the defining feature of a customary marriage.

questions.question:
Use the map shown below to answer this question.

In which direction is the river flowing to?
questions.explanation: The compass shows north as 'up'; the river runs from the high ground of the Bie Plateau on the left to the low-lying delta on the right, i.e. from west to east.

questions.question:
Study the pictures below.

Which traditional role of women is depicted in the conversation above?
questions.explanation: The mother's question and the father's remark both centre on women being expected to look after children — the traditional role of raising children.

questions.question: The feature found at grid reference 1624 is a
questions.explanation: The symbol at grid square 1624 is labelled 'Nab Fm', a farm.

questions.question: A school is found in grid reference
questions.explanation: The school ('Sch') symbol sits in the grid square with south-west corner 17 easting, 24 northing, i.e. grid reference 1724.

questions.question:
Leruo is carrying out a study to find out the time it takes for garbage to rot at a dumping site.

Which of the following data collection methods would be suitable for Leruo's study?
questions.explanation: Measuring how long garbage takes to rot requires watching and recording changes over time, which is observation.

questions.question:
Thabo has just arrived in Washington and wishes to visit the Botswana Embassy. He is given a map to locate the Embassy.

Which of the following map attributes would help Thabo to identify the Embassy?
questions.explanation: The key (legend) explains what each symbol on the map represents, including the one marking the Embassy.

questions.question: Which document can Thabo present at the police office in Washington to prove he is a Motswana?
questions.explanation: A national passport is the travel document that proves nationality/citizenship while abroad; an Omang (national ID) is not valid outside Botswana.
